Title
 Standard Test Method for Sulfate 
 Ion in Water, Waste Water, Industrial Water
Introduction

This 
 method 
 outlines the testing procedure P1, which must be performed every one week as 
 indicated by W1 in the above title block.

This method covers 
 the determination of sulfate ion in water and waste water, and industrial 
 water 10 to 100 mg / Liter (ppm) of sulfate ion ( SO4--).

This 
 document initiated by Chem. Ola Abdel Fatah Mohamed & reviewed by director 
 Chem.
 Maha 
 Mohamed Saad Hamouda, revised by quality control Chemist Waiel Ahmed 
 Tantawy at EDEPCo, and approved by Eng: Awad M. Fatthy Head Sector of 
 Talkha PS,

Also 
 reviewed by Chem. Olfat Mohamed Salah Eldeen from CCL, tested by Chemist Aza 
 Saad Abdel Wahab from CCL, and approved by Chem. Mohamed Abdel Hafez Head 
 Sector of Central Chemical Laboratories.
Significance

This method is intended for rapid routine or control tests for sulfate ion in industrial water where extreme accuracy and precision are not required. It is directly applicable over the range of l0 to 100 mg / liter (ppm) of sulfate ion (SO4--).
Summary of method

Sulfate ion is converted to a barium sulfate suspension under controlled conditions. Glycerin solution and a sodium chloride solution is added to stabilize the suspension and minimize interferences. The resulting turbidity is determined by photoelectric colorimeter or spectrophotometer and compared to a curve prepared from standard sulfate solutions.
Interferences

Insoluble suspended 
matter in the sample must be removed. Dark colors that can not be compensated for in the procedure interfere with the measurement of suspended barium sulfate ( BaSO4 ).

Although other ions normally found in water do not appear to interfere, the formation of the barium sulfate suspension is very critical. This method is more suitable as a control procedure where concentration and type of impurities present in the water are relatively constant.
Safety Precautions

items:
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.

The sample must be kept away from exposure to direct 
 sunlight.

Acids such 
 as sulfuric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep these 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Don't 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment
Apparatus

Photometer- 
 A filter photometer or spectrophotometer suitable for measurements between 350 
 and 425 nm, the preferable wavelength range being 380 to 400 nm. The cell for 
 the instrument should have a light path through the sample of approximately 40 
 mm, and should hold about 50 ml of sample.
Reagent

Glycerin Solution (1 + 1)-
Mix 1 volume of glycerin with 1 volume of 
water.

Sodium Chloride Solution 240 g/liter-
Dissolve 240 g of sodium chloride (NaCl) in water containing 20 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid ( HCl,sp gr 1.19 ) and dilute to 1 liter with water. Filter the solution if turbid .

Sulfate Standard Solution (l ml = 0.l mg SO4--)-
Dissolve 0.1479 g of anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) in water, and dilute with water to 1 liter in a volumetric flask.

Purity of 
 Reagents- All reagents shall conform 
 to the specification of the Committee on Analytical Reagents of the American 
 Chemical Society, where such specification is available. Other grades may be 
 used that the reagent is of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without 
 lessening the accuracy of the determination.
Work to be Carried Out
Calibration

Follow the 
 next procedure, using appropriate amounts of the standard sulfate solution and prepare a calibration curve showing sulfate ion content in milligrams per liter plotted against the corresponding photometer readings.

Prepare standards by diluting with water 0.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0 and 50.0 ml of standard sulfate solution to 50 ml volumes in volumetric flasks. These solutions will have sulfate ion concentrations of 0.0, 
 4.0, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 60.0, 80.0 and 100.0 mg / liter (ppm) respectively.

Note: A separate calibration curve must be prepared for each photometer and a new curve must be prepared if it is necessary to change the cell, lamp or filter, or if any other alterations of instrument or reagents are made.
Check the curve with each series of tests by running two or more solutions of known sulfate concentrations.
Procedure

Filter the sample if it 
 is turbid and adjust the temperature to be between 15 and 30oC.

Pipette into a 200 ml beaker 50 ml or less of the clear sample containing between 0.5 and 5 mg of sulfate ion. Dilute to 50 ml with water if required, add 10.0 ml of glycerin solution and 5.0 ml of NaCl solution.

Fill a 40 mm sample 
cell with sample solution, wipe it with a clean, dry cloth and place it in the cell compartment. Set the colorimeter 
to zero absorbance ( 100 % transmission ) for a blank. This compensates for any 
acid insoluble matter that has not been filtered or for color present or for 
both.

Pour the sample solution from the cell back into the beaker and add, with stirring, 0.3 g of BaCl2.2H2O crystals. Continue gently stirring the solution for l min. Let it stand for 4 min, and stir again for 15 
s.

Fill the sample cell 
as before, and immediately make a reading with the photometer.

If interferences are 
suspected, dilute sample with an equal volume of water, and determine the 
sulfate concentration again. If the value so determined is one-half that in the 
undiluted sample, interferences may be assumed to be absent.

sections.text: Calculation

Convert the photometer readings obtained with the sample to 
mg /liter sulfate ion ( SO4--) by use of the calibration 
curve described above (in calibration).
Precision

The precision of this method depends on the interferences present and the skill of the analyst. When no interfering substances are present, a careful analyst can obtain a precision of 5 % of the SO4-- or 2 mg/L whichever is greater.
